epics.name: Order export
epics.description: Let customers download their paid orders as a CSV file from their account page.

stories.iWant: to export my paid orders as a CSV file
stories.soThat: I have a record of my purchases
stories.title: Export paid orders to CSV
stories.description: From the account page, the customer downloads a CSV file with one row per paid order: order number, date, total amount including VAT. Cancelled orders are excluded. The file is named orders-YYYY-MM-DD.csv. Open point from the spec: the delimiter (comma or semicolon) and the file encoding are not decided.
acceptanceCriteria: Given a signed-in customer with paid and cancelled orders, When they request the export from their account page, Then they download a CSV file with one row per paid order and no cancelled order
Given the exported file, When the customer opens it, Then each row contains the order number, the date and the total amount including VAT
Given an export made on 16 November 2026, When the file is downloaded, Then it is named orders-2026-11-16.csv
Given a signed-in customer with no paid order, When they request the export, Then they download a file containing only the header row
stories.aiReadyReason: Which delimiter (comma or semicolon) and which encoding should the CSV file use?

tasks.title: Select the customer's paid orders
tasks.description: Query the signed-in customer's paid orders, excluding cancelled ones.

tasks.title: Generate the CSV file
tasks.description: Write the header and one row per order (number, date, total including VAT) and name the file orders-YYYY-MM-DD.csv. Depends on the missing decision: delimiter and encoding.

tasks.title: Add the export action to the account page
tasks.description: Download button that triggers the export for the signed-in customer.

tasks.title: Test the acceptance criteria
tasks.description: Tests for the exclusion of cancelled orders, the columns, the file name and the no-order case.
